claims.claim: Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle: lead with the answer, group supporting points in threes or fours that answer why or how, keep groups MECE, and open with situation, complication and question.
claims.source: Secondary summaries (BetterUp, ModelThinkers, thinkinsights.net, StrategyCase) found by search on 13 November 2026; the book itself was not checked.

concept_html:
Leaders read the first lines of what you send and decide from those. If your conclusion sits in paragraph six, most of them never reach it. Write top-down instead.

The pyramid. Put your answer, the governing thought, first. Under it, give three or four supporting points. Each one answers the question "why?" or "how?" that the answer raises. Under each point, put its evidence. The points form a MECE group (lesson F1-L1): no overlap, nothing missing.

The opening: situation, complication, question. Before the answer, give the reader just enough context:

  • Situation: what the reader already knows and accepts. "We report attrition to the board each quarter."
  • Complication: what changed. "Voluntary attrition rose from 9% to 13% this year."
  • Question: what the complication raises. "What is driving it, and what should we do?"
  • Answer: your governing thought. "One site closure explains most of the rise. The underlying rate is flat."

Keep the situation short. Readers skip what they already know.

Headings that say something. Write each heading or slide title as a full-sentence takeaway: "First-year leavers are flat since March". A heading such as "Findings" tells the reader nothing.

The skim test. Read only the first sentence of each paragraph. If the argument still holds, the structure works.

The method is Barbara Minto's, from The Pyramid Principle.

lines: Subject: Attrition rise is the Leeds closure. Underlying rate is flat
Voluntary attrition rose from 9% to 13% this year. The Leeds site closure
explains 3.5 points of the 4. Excluding it, the rate is flat at 9.5%.
1. Leeds leavers peaked in the two months after the closure was announced.
2. First-year leavers are flat since onboarding changed in March.
3. Exit reasons outside Leeds match last year's.
Recommendation: report attrition with and without site closures from Q1.

notes.html: The subject line is the governing thought. A reader who stops here has the answer.
The complication and the answer, with the size of the effect.
Three supporting points, each answering "why do you say that?"
A decision the reader can approve.

example.takeaway_html: Put the answer first, then three or four MECE points that support it, then the evidence. Open with situation, complication and question, and write headings as takeaways.

title: Lead with the answer, write in a pyramid
why_html: A data scientist sent the executive team a twelve-slide deck that built up to its recommendation on slide eleven. The chief people officer read the first three slides between meetings and asked for "the bottom line". A one-line answer in the email body, with three supporting points, would have got the decision that week.
